place_fields.vibe: Historic Deccan fort complex with Bahmani-era palaces, gateways, gardens and Indo-Islamic architectural details.
place_fields.summary: A major medieval fort in Bidar known for Bahmani architecture, Rangeen Mahal, Solah Khamba Mosque and extensive ramparts.

planning_attributes.description: Bidar Fort was completed in 1432 under Sultan Ahmad Shah Wali Bahmani and contains palaces, mosques, gardens and defensive bastions.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The fort is a major monument of the Bahmani Sultanate and later Deccan history; Karnataka Tourism highlights its completion in 1432 and its Persian garden.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Reach Bidar by road or rail from Hyderabad and Bengaluru; local taxis and buses serve the fort area.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Karnataka Tourism advises checking for restoration closures and notes visitor hours of 9 AM to 6 PM.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Wear comfortable footwear for walking around the fort and avoid visits during heavy rain.
planning_attributes.notes: The complex includes Rangeen Mahal, Solah Khamba Mosque, Takht Mahal, Gagan Mahal and a Hammam.

place_fields.vibe: Quiet lakeside setting with green fields and birdlife, suited to short walks and sunrise viewing.
place_fields.summary: Bheemasandra Lake is a lake near Tumakuru associated with surrounding greenery and birdlife; visitor reports also note damp surfaces and water-quality concerns.

planning_attributes.description: Bheemasandra Lake lies in the Bheemasandra area near Tumakuru and is visited for its lakeside scenery and birdlife.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: A visitor report places the lake about 5 km from Tumakuru; buses toward Gubbi stop at Bheemasandra Cross, followed by a walk to the lake.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Do not swim; visitor reports describe the water as drainage water and warn about damp surfaces and high shrubs, especially at night.
planning_attributes.notes: The lake is associated with nearby Melekote Lake and is used by surrounding agriculture; a water-treatment facility is also associated with the lake area.

place_fields.vibe: Quiet rural lake setting with fresh air, greenery and seasonal water flow; relatively off the beaten track.
place_fields.summary: Gulur Kere is a lake in Gulur near Tumakuru, with local reports describing a scenic setting, water flow and a small waterfall area.

planning_attributes.description: Gulur Kere is a lake in Gulur, Tumakuru, with a scenic rural setting and local recreational use.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: A Karnataka Itihasa Academy account identifies Bheema Samudra in Gulur as a Hoysala-era tank attributed to chieftain Gulibaachideva and associated with ancient sculptures on its banks.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The lake is in Gulur, Tumakuru; Yappe places Tumkur railway station about 3.33 km away.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Local reviews report muddy/slushy access after rain and heavy water flow; use care on the approach and near the water.
planning_attributes.notes: Local reports describe the area as relatively uncrowded and mention a waterfall/pour-over section and birdlife.
